text:
maria: Quick follow-up from the RFC review - we need a compact operator runbook that covers: decision TTL, provenance, and safe drain semantics for automatic fallbacks. Drafted a few items, want quick gut-checks.

owen: Love the focus. Decision TTL is critical. If a detector fires then is processed 10m later (due to retry/backlog) we must ignore it. Suggest decision_ttl_seconds and an evaluated_at timestamp in the payload.

maria: Agreed. Draft payload fields: service, route, decision_id, trigger_ts, evaluated_at, decision_ttl_seconds, action (switch|drain|noop), target (optional), provenance: {detector_id, rule_version, probe_ids}, signals (map of name->value), trace_id, request_sample_hash.

lee: Small ask: avoid nested objects per emitter constraints — provenance can be a single string like "detector:detector_id|ver:1.2|probes:pid1,pid2". Easier to index and stable across languages.

sasha: Also: include decision_lifetime_state: proposed|executing|completed|aborted to help dashboards show where decisions hang.

maria: Good point. We'll keep provenance encoded, and add a decision_state field. Also add decision_attempt integer so retries are visible.

owen: For drain semantics: default behavior should be graceful drain for N seconds (configurable per-service), then hard switch. Ops runbook should instruct to extend drain window if tail latency heavy.

sasha: Telemetry names proposal: fallback.decisions.count, fallback.decisions.latency_ms, fallback.decisions.state_change, fallback.triggers.count, fallback.triggers.reason. Use snake or dot? dots are nicer for dashboards.

lee: Dots are fine. Ensure metrics emitter has unit tests that assert exact strings. I'll add that to my PR.

maria: Minimal ops playbook (short):
1) On alert, open fallback decision panel -> find decision_id.
2) Inspect decision_state and provenance string.
3) If decision_state == executing and stalled > 60s, run manual drain extend: POST /ops/internal/decisions/{decision_id}/extend with body {extend_seconds: 300}.
4) If decision aborted repeatedly (abort_count > 2 in 15m), revert detector -> set detector.disable=true and trigger manual canary pin.

owen: Manual API example (ops-only):
```bash
# extend running decision drain
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"extend_seconds":300}' \
  https://ops-api.internal.redwood/internal/decisions/dec-1745678901/extend
```

lee: For traceability, every decision event must attach a link to the trace URL if available, e.g. trace_url field. Don't attach raw payloads.

sasha: Alert rule: fire if fallback.decisions.state_change:aborted AND fallback.decisions.count > 1 in 10m. Pager to infra oncall. Lower-severity if just triggers spike but no state changes.

maria: Postmortem checklist snippet to include: collect decision payloads, probe logs for detector_id, correlated traces (trace_id), canary traffic samples, and recent model-eval snapshots. Save metadata in incident ticket (decision_id tag).

deploy-bot: deploy: Canary-policy update pushed to staging: default_drains_seconds=120.

owen: Last item: make sure the Decision API returns a canonical decision_id on success and the timestamp evaluated_at. API should be idempotent by decision_id so replays don't create duplicates.

maria: I'll author the runbook with these constraints and encode provenance as compact string. Will add sample payload and the curl examples. Will PR to runbooks repo and ping docs team for dashboards.

lee: I'll add emitter tests and a linter rule to ban dynamic metric name assembly.

sasha: I'll own alert rules and the dashboard panels.

maria: Great. I'll post the PR link here once created. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
